cases.headline: Breakdown (shadow short) in a Weak market
cases.bull:
**Bull case for the DLR shadow short (entry 162.46, stop 179.05): honest but modest.**

**Trend and stage.** The setup is a clean Stage 3 to 4 transition. The close of 162.46 is 8.9% below the SMA50 and 11.1% below the SMA200. It sits 21% off the 52-week high, with 63-day and 126-day returns of -13.3% and -14.3%. The lower highs are visible: 200.89 in April, 197.72 in July, 198.79 in August, 186.13 in November.

**Breakdown quality.** Today's candle opened at 173.09 and closed at 162.46, near its 162.21 low. That is a drop of about 6.6% on 3.62M shares, a volume ratio of 1.59. It cleared the October support area (the 167.17 low on 10/15 and 168.52 on 10/22) decisively. The base is 26 sessions long and 11.3% deep, and the support floor it broke had held through several tests.

**Relative strength.** The Mansfield figure is -9.46 and the RS rank is 26. DLR's 63-day return of -13.3% compares with -6.2% for the benchmark, so it is lagging by about 7 points. The market regime is Weak, with the benchmark below a falling 200-day and stage 2 share at 48.8%. The tape favors the short side.

**Stop and target.** The stop at 179.05 is 10.2% above entry, roughly 2.5 ATR (ATR is 4.1%). It sits above the November swing highs near 183 only partly, so a tighter stop at about 175 to 176 (above the 11/19 and 11/20 range) is defensible. The first target is the 52-week low area. From_lo52 is +13.4%, which puts the low near 143. That is about 12% below entry, a reward of roughly 1.2R against the 179.05 stop.

**Against me, plainly.** The track record is poor. Same grade has n=60 with average R of -0.46 and a 28% win rate. Same grade and regime has n=32 with average R of -0.97 and a 9% win rate. The most similar cases have n=25 with average R of -0.53. A VIX of 35.89 invites violent squeezes, as the 7/24 spike to 206 showed (+11% in a day).

**What proves me wrong:** a close back above about 174 (the 11/20 open) within a few sessions, or any reclaim of 180.
cases.bear:
As the Bear, my job is to argue against the short, and I'll note where the numbers fall short of that.

**Track record is the wrong way round for my case.** The screen's earlier down signals lost money: same grade n=60, avg R -0.46, win 28%, median return -2.5%. In the Weak regime n=32, avg R -0.97, win 9%, median return -9.2%. Here "win" appears to mean the short lost, so this is not a clean base rate against the short. The sign convention is unclear, which weakens everything above. I won't lean on it, but it is a warning that the screen has no proven edge.

**The case against shorting now:**
- **Late and extended.** Price closed at 162.46, down 8.9% from the SMA50 and 11.1% from the SMA200. The last bar ran from 174.02 to 162.46, about -6.6% in one session. Shorting after a 6.6% drop risks a bounce.
- **Stop is wide.** The stop at 179.05 is 16.6 above entry, about 10.2% and 2.5 ATR (ATR 4.08%). On $1,000 at 0.5% risk ($5), the position is about $49, roughly 0.3 shares. A cash account cannot short anyway, so this is only a shadow trade.
- **Panic backdrop.** VIX is 35.89. Vol spikes often reverse sharply, and DLR has shown this: it gapped from 178.12 to 197.72 on 2026-07-24 on 10.8M volume, a +11% move. A gap like that against a short would blow through the stop.
- **Relative weakness is already priced in.** RS rank 26, Mansfield -9.46, 63-day return -13.3% against a benchmark of -6.2%.
- **Range support.** The 52-week low is only 13% below, and the 10-15 to 10-22 lows near 167-169 were bought repeatedly before this break.

**What supports the short, honestly:** the close is below the 167.17 pivot, which is also the 10-15 low. Volume is 3.6M against roughly 2M typical, and the regime is Weak with the benchmark below a falling 200-day average. Stage 3 topping is consistent with a break.

**What would change my mind:** a follow-through close below about 160 on steady volume, or a failed bounce that stalls under 167-170. Either would make the short cleaner. Without that, I would skip it.

judge.title: Avoid
judge.text: DLR has rolled over from a top near 200 in April through August. It is now 8.9% below its 50-day average and 11.1% below its 200-day, and down 13.3% over three months. For about five weeks it held a floor near 167-169, then broke through it on 11/20 with one 6.6% drop to 162.46. That day's volume was 1.59 times normal. It is lagging the index, which is down 6.2% over the same three months, in a weak market with the VIX near 36.
reasons_for: Price closed at 162.46, below the 167.17 pivot and the October lows, on volume 1.59x its average. The break is real.
The trend is down. The stock is -8.9% vs its SMA50 and -11.1% vs its SMA200, with lower highs at 200.89, 198.79 and 186.13.
Relative strength is poor: RS rank 26, Mansfield -9.46, and a 63-day return of -13.3% against -6.2% for the benchmark.
The market regime is Weak, with the benchmark below a falling 200-day average and stage-2 share at 48.8%.
reasons_against: This screen's down signals have lost on average. Same grade: n=60, avg R -0.46, 28% win. Same grade in a Weak regime: n=32, avg R -0.97, 9% win. Most similar cases: n=25, avg R -0.53. Nothing in this setup shows why it would differ.
The entry is late. A single 6.6% drop to 162.46 leaves price stretched at -8.9% from the SMA50, which invites a snap-back.
With the VIX at 35.89, squeezes are likely. DLR jumped about 11% in one day on 7/24, from 178.12 to 197.72, which would blow through any sensible stop.
The screen's stop at 179.05 is 10.2% away, about 2.5 ATR. A tighter stop near 174.5 needs a target near 144, close to the 52-week low (~143). That leaves little room beyond a 1.5R payoff.
The account is a long-only cash account, so this can only be a shadow trade. There is no reason to force it.
judge.invalidation: For the shadow short, a close back above 174.5 (the 11/20 open and high area near 174) would void the breakdown. Separately, a close above 180, a reclaim of the November range, would show the break failed.
